content.text:
The separate command rebuilds the stored funder grouping from data already in the database. It originally existed to **backfill existing databases** when grouping was introduced; PR #52 explicitly gives that reason. Normal declaration loading already refreshes groups automatically, including unchanged-data retries. [PR #52](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/52)

It also lets you apply **grouping-policy changes without importing declarations again**. Reviewed families and preferred names are compiled into Rust, while HTTP handlers read the stored grouping results. PR #57 explicitly says policy changes require a rebuild and projection refresh. [PR #57](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/57)

So the evidence suggests it is an operational shortcut for recomputing derived data independently of ingestion. Having a separate CLI command is one way to provide that capability; the record does **not** establish that it must be manual, or explain why it was chosen over an automatic startup or deployment step.

- **Source control:** PRs #28, #34, #43, #52, #57; grouping and declaration-loading code.
- **Issue tracker:** all three issues and searches for funder groups, grouping, and refresh; no direct rationale.
